I used to love this extension. It worked perfectly fine. Then the recent update ruined it. 

I work fast paced in multiple tabs, constantly having to copy and paste from tab to tab. 
Now switching between past tabs will sometimes take me to another opened window. 
It's now become quicker to use mouse clicks than to use this extension.

Please allow a separate option for 2 - 4 tabs. I see some others might need this. I just need a back and forth from just the last tab I visited. 
And especially take out the option to switch to a different window. Or at the very least make it a feature you can turn on or off. I am constantly taken to a new window of tabs I haven't touched in a while. Meaning I have to click on the tab I want to go to. Defeating the purpose of the extension. 

Once again, the last version was perfect. This version made me turn it off until it's updated in Chrome.

reviews.text:
New issue after the 2023 Nov Chrome update: It doesn't work for tabs that are in Group and have Save Group turned on. 
--
It works. The only issue is that the rendering of the browsing history is delayed by 1 or 2 sec, and it didn't keep track of Alt key. So if I press and release Alt+S twice within 2 second, it will not switch between current page and the last page. And, if I press Alt+S and releasing S but holding Alt, it will not continue cycling to the previous page when I press S again. (Basically, it didn't behave like the Alt + Tab in Windows.)
reviews.dev_reply:
This is due to limitation enforced by Chrome API. You can read more in the FAQ.
You keep Alt pressed or not, it is based on the delay between presses. Hope it helps.

The longer version explanation - Chrome API will not tell individually if Alt key is pressed or not. It only lets you know whenever a combination is pressed for e.g. Alt + S.

Dear Developer,

Thank you for creating CLUT. I have been playtesting version 2.1 recently and wanted to share some constructive feedback. Software evolution is infinite, and even highly useful tools can always be refined and optimised further.

The core concept of mapping tabs using a three-point anchor system is an excellent foundation. The underlying switching logic works well, but there are a few minor adjustments that could elevate the overall user experience and streamline the system.

During my testing, I noticed an occasional bug where an entirely unrelated window is pulled into focus. This seems particularly noticeable when using the Alt+S and Alt+Shift+S shortcuts, which currently feel a bit unpredictable compared to the primary quick switch.

Additionally, the inclusion of a slower switch and a reverse direction might be slightly redundant for a standard workflow. Simplifying the extension by focusing on a single, highly reliable shortcut could make it much more intuitive. A potential solution could be to resolve the window-focusing bug in Alt+S and adopt its pacing as the primary switching speed, as the Alt+W quick switch can sometimes feel a bit too rapid.

I really appreciate the effort and time you have put into this project to replicate such an essential workflow feature. I hope these suggestions are helpful for your next round of updates.
